from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Geometric Intuition: The 'Infinite Zoom' and Tangents"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Now, let's look at a curving roller coaster.",
            "The slope changes at every point along the track.",
            "Zooming in closer, the curve begins to flatten.",
            "Eventually, it looks just like a straight line.",
            "This \"local line\" is the tangent to the curve."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Color definitions
        CURVE_YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        TANGENT_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        HIGHLIGHT_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Now, let's look at a curving roller coaster.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CURVE_YELLOW)
        
        # Load SVG Asset (Issue 26)
        # L009: Use SVGMobject for designated asset paths
        roller_coaster = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/roller.svg")
        roller_coaster.set_color(CURVE_YELLOW)
        roller_coaster.set_stroke(width=3)
        
        # VGroup for graph elements to be zoomed (Issue 35 & 36)
        graph_group = VGroup(roller_coaster)
        
        # Positioning: Use area C2 to F5 and scale 0.5 to prevent overlap with lecture (Issues 35 & 36)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "C2", "F5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(roller_coaster), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The slope changes at every point along the track.
        # Mark a point P on the curve.
        
        # We need a path for the sliding dot and for point P. 
        # SVGMobjects are typically VGroups; we target the primary path.
        path_for_dot = roller_coaster[0] if isinstance(roller_coaster, VGroup) and len(roller_coaster) > 0 else roller_coaster
        
        prop_p = 0.65 # Selected proportion for point P along the curve
        point_p_pos = path_for_dot.point_from_proportion(prop_p)
        point_p = Dot(point_p_pos, color=HIGHLIGHT_WHITE, radius=0.08)
        
        # Label P (L003: within 1 grid unit of target)
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=24, color=HIGHLIGHT_WHITE)
        label_p.next_to(point_p, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Demonstration dot sliding along the curve
        sliding_dot = Dot(color=HIGHLIGHT_WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        # Move along path to illustrate changing slope
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(sliding_dot, path_for_dot), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(FadeOut(sliding_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Zooming in closer, the curve begins to flatten.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(CURVE_YELLOW)
        
        # Magnifying glass circle at point P
        mag_glass = Circle(radius=0.6, color=HIGHLIGHT_WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        mag_glass.move_to(point_p.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(mag_glass))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Zoom Stage 1: Scale around P
        zoom_factor_1 = 5.0
        # L015: Prevent label overlap by scaling and positioning relative to the zoom
        self.play(
            graph_group.animate.scale(zoom_factor_1, about_point=point_p.get_center()),
            mag_glass.animate.scale(1.8),
            label_p.animate.scale(0.7).next_to(point_p, UR, buff=0.05),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Eventually, it looks just like a straight line.
        # Zoom Stage 2: Very high magnification to "flatten" the curve visually
        zoom_factor_2 = 6.0
        self.play(
            graph_group.animate.scale(zoom_factor_2, about_point=point_p.get_center()),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This "local line" is the tangent to the curve.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(TANGENT_BLUE)
        
        # Calculate local tangent orientation from points near P on the scaled path
        # L013: Using point_from_proportion for coordinate mapping
        p1 = path_for_dot.point_from_proportion(max(0, prop_p - 0.0001))
        p2 = path_for_dot.point_from_proportion(min(1, prop_p + 0.0001))
        tangent_direction = normalize(p2 - p1)
        
        # Create blue tangent line (Issue 36: aligned with the flattened curve)
        tangent_line = Line(
            start=point_p.get_center() - 3.5 * tangent_direction,
            end=point_p.get_center() + 3.5 * tangent_direction,
            color=TANGENT_BLUE,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        # Highlight with Indicate (L004)
        self.play(Indicate(tangent_line, color=TANGENT_BLUE))
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title Setup
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture_group = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)
        self.add(self.lecture_group)

        # Define animation grid for the right side of the screen
        # x ranges from roughly 1.0 to 6.0, y ranges from -3.0 to 2.0
        self.grid_map = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Calculate coordinates for the right half of the canvas
                x_coord = 1.5 + (j * 0.8)
                y_coord = 2.0 - (i * 0.8)
                self.grid_map[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_coord, y_coord, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Helper to place mobjects on the defined grid."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid_map:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid_map[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Define content for the scene
        title_content = "The Rhythm of Change: Derivative Formulas"
        bullets = [
            "- Power Rule: d/dx [x^n] = n*x^(n-1)",
            "- Constant Rule: d/dx [c] = 0",
            "- Sum Rule: (f+g)' = f' + g'",
            "- Geometric Interpretation",
            "- Slope of the Tangent Line"
        ]

        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title_content, bullets)

        # Visual Demonstration on the Right side
        # Create a coordinate system in the grid area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": BLUE, "include_tip": False}
        )
        # Position axes in the middle of the right grid area
        axes.move_to(self.grid_map["C4"])
        
        # Plot a simple parabola segment
        parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[0, 2.5], color=YELLOW)
        
        # Tangent line logic
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 2), color=RED)
        tangent = Line(
            start=axes.c2p(1, 0), 
            end=axes.c2p(3, 4), 
            color=WHITE, 
            stroke_width=2
        )

        # Display Animations
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(parabola), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.wait(1)

        # Highlighting the Power Rule Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} x^n = n x^{n-1}", color=GOLD).scale(1.1)
        # Move formula to the bottom right grid area
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "F3")
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        
        # Move objects to grid positions to demonstrate grid functionality
        self.play(
            dot.animate.move_to(self.grid_map["A6"]),
            formula.animate.move_to(self.grid_map["B6"]).scale(0.7),
            run_time=2
        )

        self.wait(2)
